<description>
`btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` stores blocks that bitcoind skips when it did not request them. It processes every block as if requested. A block is therefore stored even if it has less work than the tip, is more than 288 blocks ahead of it, is below the minimum chain work, or was pruned before. I document that a caller taking blocks from untrusted sources must apply these checks itself. I leave the header path undocumented, as discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33822#discussion_r2592425740. #34022, which proposed removing the flag, was closed. Blocks differ because `force_processing` changes what is stored.

The second commit documents two preconditions that abort the process. `btck_precomputed_transaction_data_create` aborts when `spent_outputs` is set and its length differs from the input count. A nested `btck_chainstate_manager_import_blocks` call on the same chainstate manager also aborts. I checked both aborts with a small program against the library. The kernel library builds, and the whitespace and commit-message lints pass.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
ed2c4a344a kernel: document that process_block stores unrequested blocks

btck_chainstate_manager_process_block processes every block as
requested. Validation therefore does not skip a block that has less
work than the tip, is more than 288 blocks ahead of it, is below the
minimum chain work, or was pruned before. bitcoind skips such blocks
when it did not ask for them.

The API does not say so. Document that a caller taking blocks from
untrusted sources has to apply these checks itself.

dda2c1f325 kernel: document two aborting preconditions

btck_precomputed_transaction_data_create aborts when spent_outputs is
set and its length differs from the number of inputs. A nested
btck_chainstate_manager_import_blocks call on the same chainstate
manager also aborts. The header states neither.

I add both to the header. I keep the asserts, since #35312 treats
invalid arguments as programmer errors.
</commits>
